verdict.why: The structural cost hurdle is decisive: a flat Rs 15.93 DP charge on a Rs 1,000 delivery trade creates a ~1.8% round-trip breakeven before any market move, and a 20% short-term capital gains tax applies to any profit within 12 months. With only 23 trading days to horizon, the single affordable candidate (CUB.NS) carries RBI rate-sensitivity and an earnings date (Nov 2) just outside the window that could trigger a gap move. The three CASH votes correctly identify that no risk-adjusted edge reliably clears this cost barrier in such a short horizon; Kimi's bullish case relies on analyst targets that historically lag price and ignores the tax drag. Preserving the Rs 1,000 intact avoids locking in near-certain frictional losses.
verdict.dissent: Kimi K3 voted CUB.NS citing a 12.5% mean-target upside and relative strength, but did not net out the 1.8% round-trip cost plus 20% STCG tax (effective hurdle ~4%), nor address the event risk of a post-horizon earnings gap.
verdict.what_would_change_our_mind: A budget increase to ~Rs 10,000+ (making the flat DP charge negligible), a longer horizon (3+ months) to amortize costs, or a clear pre-earnings momentum setup with a defined catalyst inside the window.
